overview.text: Shielded Labs (aquietinvestor) opens by announcing incentivized Crosslink feature nets: 500 ZEC in total, 25 ZEC for the first season, cTAZ rewards split 40% miners, 40% stakers and 20% Dev Fund, and a staged roadmap whose mainnet activation follows existing governance (#1). Most early replies are sign-ups. dontbeevil is confident the dev fund will not be extended and recommends obtaining strong signals and support for Crosslink (#5, #6); Shielded Labs replies that testnets should be permissionless and need no coinholder approval, while it will not push for activation without support (#8). hiroprotagonist is undecided but approves of testing first (#26), and gigantes wants critics to offer alternatives on probabilistic finality (#27).

Season 1 starts on April 15 with a workshop and instructions (#15, #19). Users report bugs (#24, #34, #40), and v3 and v4 follow (#31, #33). In May finality stalls when stake goes offline (#38). A six-week review calls the network extremely rough, says Shielded Labs will work through stalls live rather than reset, and replaces fixed seasons with rolling six-week payouts (#39). Kenbak and zk_nd3r say the v6 visibility tooling and live handling helped (#40, #42).

Round 1 payouts: after a viewing-key deadline (#47), 11.2 ZEC went to 22 recipients and 13.8 ZEC to discretionary rewards (#49). alphiz22 says they submitted both viewing keys on time and were not paid, and supplies backup evidence (#48, #50, #52, #59). Shielded Labs found nothing in the scan, then said the Orchard actions cannot be decrypted by either key, show no staking actions, the block hashes do not match and the mining address is the faucet's, while staking since block 131,000 counts for Round 2 (#51, #62). Separately, philthefirst asks about a default miner address and plaintext seeds in snapshots (#54); zk_nd3r finds no seed in the archive (#55, #56), samhsmith explains the faucet wallet (#57), and philthefirst accepts it (#60).

Ahead of Round 2, Shielded Labs says there will be no reset and announces a canonical block to verify against (#67, #72). alphiz22 reports a node stuck at block 137,307 and takes refused BFT connections as proof of a network-wide stall (#68); samhsmith answers that the port is UDP and the node is probably on a side chain or hit a bad block (#69), and alphiz22 accepts the UDP point (#71). ZKZeek asks what incentives surface (#73), and Shielded Labs says mainly a larger engaged group (#74). alphiz22 submits a security report (#75); philliptrudeau doubts the cited line caused the crashes and ranks latent gaps as low priority (#76).

From August the thread fills with community tooling: staker.space (#85), Uscmigs' indexer analyses (#87), Nozy operator notes (#89, #90) and the 0scan tracker (#114). Shielded Labs announces plans to reset the network regularly and a Nightly Network (#83), then a new network for Round 3 (#101, #113). Sl145 reports a Round 2 stall lasting hours (#102, #105); strahncryptography calls such pauses common (#103); Sl145 accepts that but keeps the duration worth documenting (#104). Round 2 payouts complete in #117.

positions.label: Shielded Labs: build and test Crosslink openly on feature nets
positions.summary: Testnets are permissionless and give the community a working product to evaluate; mainnet activation still needs broad support. An incentivized net draws many more testers. Stalls are expected BFT behavior, best worked through live with better tooling. Latent gaps in prototype code rank behind other features.

positions.label: Seek community support before heavy investment
positions.summary: Given the effort and resources going into Crosslink, Shielded Labs should obtain strong signals and support for it. Confident the dev fund will not be extended and that any proposal would go to a coinholder vote.

positions.label: Wants alternatives to probabilistic finality
positions.summary: Criticism of Crosslink is fine, but critics should propose other fixes; denying the finality problem would leave private money subject to PoW miners reversing transactions. Another poster is undecided and watching the criticism while welcoming testing first.

positions.label: Testers and tool builders: live debugging and observability
positions.summary: Participants who test and build around the feature net. zk_nd3r and Kenbak say working through rough states live and the v6 visibility tooling have helped; others publish explorers, indexers, monitors and wallet companions and report bugs, RPC gaps and data on stalls, staking and mining.

positions.label: Round 1 claimant: evidence shows participation, please re-check
positions.summary: Submitted both viewing keys on time, recovered backup evidence of staking transactions and accepted blocks, and cannot split them by wallet. Argues the ZingoDelegator version may have made Orchard transactions unreadable and that the setup guide never warned about the faucet address.

positions.label: Harden the finality path against malformed input
positions.summary: The finality path panics on a BFT proposal with an empty header list, which matches crashes seen on the author's node; two further gaps are latent, defense-in-depth issues, not a remote forgery.

positions.label: Flag possible exposures for clarification
positions.summary: A default miner address shared by nodes and plaintext seeds in public snapshots might affect many testers, so they should be checked. After replies the poster accepts the address is the faucet wallet.

positions.label: Finality pauses are routine and not worth a post
positions.summary: Such pauses are common and even expected on the feature net, like testnet reorganisations, so the report may not need a post.

positions.label: A multi-hour stall is worth documenting
positions.summary: Accepts that pauses are expected, but a stall of hours with PoW advancing, BFT peers dropping from 25-26 to 1 and a retarget that cannot take effect is worth recording for developers.

positions.label: Incentives surface finality edge cases quiet testnets miss
positions.summary: Paying real participants brings genuine load, where finality edge cases mostly show up. Asks whether stake will cluster around a few finalizers and how non-technical people can help.

summary.tldr: Running thread for Shielded Labs' incentivized Crosslink feature net: sign-ups, releases, two payout rounds, community tooling. Debate is light: whether testnets need prior community support, a disputed Round 1 payout, address and snapshot worries, and whether finality stalls are routine.
